posts.body_html: Thanks for sharing alexis! I personally think there's a lot of potential for really cool hybrids involving psittacina backcrossed 3 or 4 generations. One problem is many psitt hybrids, like ones involving wrigleyana and courtii as parents, will still have occasional folded and morphed pitchers. If you can breed that out though, the sky is the limit.

Mar 11, 2021 19:48:36 GMT -5 greenthumb said:
One problem is many psitt hybrids, like ones involving wrigleyana and courtii as parents, will still have occasional folded and morphed pitchers. If you can breed that out though, the sky is the limit.
Jerry Addington has done some sensational work breeding that out, and he's mentioned how valuable psitt is as a breeder for the longevity of the pitchers. I will say, lots of not-so-complex psitt crosses do have very attractive lids in my opinion (Hummer's Hammerhead is one of my favorite plants), and sometimes they're just so uniquely funky that it's hard not to love 'em For example, check out this gorgeous courtii x Slack by Rob Co:
